type.value: deformation twins (nanoscale twin boundaries generated during cold rolling, thermally stable after recovery annealing)

overall_structure.value: Cold rolled and annealed non-age hardenable austenitic Fe-Mn-Al-C steel: after cold rolling the material contains a large number of nanoscale deformation-twin boundaries; subsequent recovery/recrystallization annealing leaves the deformation twins thermally stable while the dislocation density is reduced, producing fine recrystallized austenitic grains and enabling cold formability together with high strength by extreme grain refinement. With increasing annealing time/temperature the recrystallized volume fraction increases, changing the yield behaviour from continuous to discontinuous yielding; a lower degree of recrystallization provides relatively high strength but lower elongation.

unmapped_findings: For non-age hardenable austenitic Fe-Mn-Al-C steels, the cold rolling + recovery/recrystallization annealing route can be run on the continuous annealing line used for producing conventional steel strips (b0107).

Strengthening in the non-precipitation hardenable (non-age hardenable) austenitic Fe-Mn-Al-C alloys is effected through solid solution hardening and by grain refinement through cold rolling and recrystallization annealing (b0304).

For the non-age hardenable austenitic cold rolled + annealed condition, effective grain refinement is caused by the generation of a large number of nanoscale twin boundaries during cold rolling; subsequent recovery annealing leaves the deformation twins thermally stable while the dislocation density is reduced, giving cold formability on the one hand and high strength by extreme grain refinement on the other (b0258).
